clue.text: Shopper features on song against contracting

parts.note: performing well, as in good form

indicators.note: contracting means shortening the word by its last letter

parts.note: against means anti, opposed to

explanation.surface: A shopper's purchases include a protest song against a building contractor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shopper' is not a buyer: in British slang to shop someone is to betray them to the police. 'contracting' trims ANTI to ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To shop someone is British slang for telling the police about them, so a shopper is a police tip-off source.

clue.text: To sum up case, happening upon it

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece placed upon another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: happening means fashionable, in
a brief is the case a barrister is given to argue

explanation.surface: A lawyer summing up a case that happened to land on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upon it' puts IN above BRIEF in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for speaking briefly, giving a summary of the main points.

clue.text: Following distressed supplies you looked for oil

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
racked means tormented, distressed

explanation.surface: After seeing someone in distress, you went looking for oil to bring them supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Fracking is a method of drilling and splitting rock to release oil or gas, so this is the past tense of searching that way.

clue.text: Fixing their air-con, a master of hot air

indicators.note: fixing an air conditioner means taking it apart and rebuilding, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An engineer repairing someone's air conditioner is an expert at producing hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot air' looks like it belongs to the air-con; it means empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is pompous, empty talk, and an expert in persuasive or showy speech fits that jokey description.

clue.text: Touching range in empty supermarket

parts.note: an AGA is a British make of cast-iron range cooker

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A kitchen range on display in a supermarket with bare shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a brand of heavy cooking stove common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: Something leaning against a wall is in contact with it, so the preposition can mean in physical contact.

clue.text: One holding guy's wine up for finish, say

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine

indicators.note: the finishing letter of the word up is wanted

parts.note: say means for example, e.g.

explanation.surface: Someone raising a glass of wine to a man's finish line, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' is not a man: it is a guy rope, which a tent peg anchors.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope steadying a tent, and the spike driven into the ground holds that rope fast.

clue.text: Has a butcher's announced results in London accountant!

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: butcher's hook is rhyming slang for look, so has a butcher's means takes a look, peeps

explanation.surface: A butcher announces the results of something to a London accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: The diarist's name is traditionally said 'peeps'. 'accountant' is not about money: he wrote an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pepys kept the famous diary of 1660s London life, so he gave an account of the city.

clue.text: Take stone from mine

definitions.meaning: to remove the stone from a fruit such as a cherry
a coal mine, a shaft dug for coal

explanation.surface: Extracting a stone from a quarry or mine.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is removing a fruit's stone; the noun is a colliery.

clue.text: Responsible pupil's second to drop Polish?

indicators.note: the second letter falls one place lower in the down light

parts.note: a prefect is a senior pupil given responsibility

explanation.surface: A prefect's deputy must stop speaking Polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the language; it is the verb, to refine. 'second to drop' moves the R one place down.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish work is to refine it until it has no flaws.

clue.text: Mark entered by school's subject

indicators.note: the first piece has the second piece put inside it

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
the plot is the subject matter of a story

explanation.surface: A school subject in which a pupil's work is marked.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot or smudge on paper is a mark, as in an ink stain.

clue.text: Two British people

parts.note: a race is a people

explanation.surface: A couple of Britons.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace is a pair, used especially of game birds.

clue.text: With nothing on relative keeping a rule out

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

indicators.note: out means put out of order

explanation.surface: A naked relative ignoring the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' means holding inside; 'out' signals the rearrangement, and the surface's 'rule out' is a false phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in a natural state, used in English for naked.

clue.text: Kind of money not in use

indicators.note: something not in the word is removed from it

parts.note: to milk something is to exploit or use it

explanation.surface: A type of currency that is no longer in circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means sort or type, as in people of that sort.

clue.text: Pervasive crackers met in person

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so these letters go wild

explanation.surface: Crackers, the snack, turned up everywhere when someone was met face to face.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everywhere at once pervades every place, which is the meaning of being present throughout.

clue.text: Exposing tip, needle nearly gets round

parts.note: a tip is an end

indicators.note: nearly means without its last letter

parts.note: to needle is to annoy, anger
a ring is round, a circle

explanation.surface: A sewing scene: the needle's point almost goes round the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposing someone to danger is putting them at risk.

clue.text: FA Cup size is beginning to trouble trendy fan

parts.note: DD is a bra cup size

indicators.note: the beginning letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: The size of the FA Cup starts to bother a football fan.
explanation.walkthrough: The FA is England's Football Association, but 'Cup' turns out to be a bra cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows every passing craze is an enthusiast of fashions, a fan of trends.

clue.text: Leave wife's hand over fair parts

parts.note: to go is to leave
old Dutch is Cockney slang for wife, from duchess

explanation.surface: A wife's hand seems to wave over a funfair's attractions as she leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' is London Cockney slang for one's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means each pays their own share of a bill, handing over an equal portion.

clue.text: After sex change, cleavage becomes goal

indicators.note: a sex change swaps F for female with M for male

parts.note: fission is splitting, cleavage

explanation.surface: Following gender reassignment, one's cleavage becomes the aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A mission is a task one sets out to achieve, an aim.

clue.text: Reserve of dye most supply

indicators.note: supply read as supple-y, in a supple way, bending the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A stockpile of dye kept by the biggest supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' looks like a store of stock; it means shyness.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve is restraint in behaviour, a reluctance to show off.

clue.text: Reportedly in the doghouse? Come on!

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so a word that sounds the same

parts.note: chez pup, French chez meaning at the home of, so at the puppy's place

explanation.surface: Someone in disgrace is being urged to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the doghouse' suggests disgrace, but is read literally as a dog's home, chez pup.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation urges someone to improve their behaviour or performance, as does the idiom.

clue.text: Solution: only one string!

definitions.meaning: a cure-all remedy, a quack's solution
with only a single string a guitarist can make ..., read as two words

explanation.surface: A one-string instrument as the answer to a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: split the answer as NO STRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack remedy is offered as the solution for an ailment, and a one-stringed guitar allows no chord strumming.

clue.text: How's eagle's made descent

parts.note: the bird's name is made by putting one letter inside four others, an instruction the answer spells when split after its first three letters

explanation.surface: A question about how an eagle came to be, answered with its ancestry.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as an instruction: L placed in EAGE makes the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, one's line of descent from forebears.

clue.text: Country people ban one-night stands

indicators.note: the answer stands within these words, held inside them

explanation.surface: Citizens prohibit casual sexual encounters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a nation on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: FIFA, say, adding China for good in business meeting

indicators.note: for means in place of, one swapped for the other

parts.note: AGM is an annual general meeting of a company
china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a crony

explanation.surface: Football's governing body adds China at a business meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: rhyming slang china plate means mate. 'adding' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed from initial letters, as FIFA is from Fédération Internationale de Football Association.

clue.text: Attempts rest of exercises, getting poor grade

indicators.note: getting means taking something inside
exercises means works over, putting these letters through their paces in a new order

parts.note: F is a failing grade

explanation.surface: Someone tries resting from exercise and gets a bad mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' rearranges REST OF, and 'getting' puts F among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tries and endeavours are attempts, the plural noun.

clue.text: Open to discovery, island lay further west

indicators.note: in an across light, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: Elba is the island of Napoleon's exile
a lay is a song or ballad
to further is to aid

explanation.surface: An island lies further west, waiting to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'further' is not a direction here but the verb to help.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition that can be identified by examination is open to being found out.

clue.text: Judge is on fire, lacking passion

parts.note: re means on, about

indicators.note: lacking means with that removed

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: A judge is fired up yet strangely dispassionate.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee adjudicates a match, judging the play.

clue.text: Wearing more satin that's for evening out

indicators.note: wearing means worn away, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Wearing more satin is the way to dress for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' looks like a night on the town; it is making cloth smooth and even.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing appliance smooths creases from clothes, levelling the fabric.

clue.text: Presenter who's driven old lady back to Bromley

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old lady

indicators.note: the back letter of the word Bromley

explanation.surface: A TV host gives his elderly mother a lift home to Bromley, a London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: James May is a motoring television host, best known for Top Gear.

clue.text: Main nerve centre hidden

indicators.note: the centre of these words holds the answer

explanation.surface: The main nerve centre is concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings are private ones, kept concealed from others.

clue.text: Rich kid's fish with fork for starter

indicators.note: for starter means in place of the first letter

parts.note: a guppy is a small aquarium fish
Y is shaped like a fork

explanation.surface: A wealthy child's pet fish gets a fork as an appetiser.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1980s term for a young urban professional describes a wealthy young person.

clue.text: I'm finally making amends for developing psychological warfare

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so these letters change order
finally means the last letter of making

explanation.surface: Someone finally apologises for starting a campaign of mental manipulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Manipulative tactics meant to unsettle an opponent mentally are a form of psychological combat.
